opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next generations of CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators.

opex.name: Marketing, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Writing down the value of technology bought in acquisitions (Xilinx above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — shown net of a $6M licensing gain.

footerNote: Cost of sales of $3,257M includes $215M of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, on top of $3,042M of cost of sales before that amortization, following AMD's own presentation of its income statement. The amortization line in operating expenses is shown as $414M — AMD's $420M of amortization net of a $6M licensing gain. The tax line was a $297M benefit, drawn as a green source into net profit (the taxben link fix used on AMD's 2024-q3 and 2025-q2 pages is applied here too).

kpis.label: Data Center revenue
kpis.note: +38% YoY — record Instinct GPU and EPYC sales

otherDetail: Other income, net of $49M (primarily interest income from short-term investments, partly offset by other effects), plus $6M of equity income from an investee, less $27M of interest expense — a net +$28M. AMD reports equity income on its own line below the tax line; following the sibling AMD pages it is folded into otherIncomeM here and disclosed in this breakdown.

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators — driven by the first Instinct MI300 GPU shipments and growth in 4th Gen EPYC CPU sales.

segments.name: Client
segments.note: Ryzen processors for PCs — up 62%, driven primarily by Ryzen 7000 Series processor sales as the PC market recovered.

segments.name: Gaming
segments.note: Graphics cards and console chips — down 17% on lower semi-custom (console) revenue, partly offset by higher Radeon GPU sales.

segments.name: Embedded
segments.note: Chips built into industrial, communications and other equipment (the Xilinx business) — down 24% as customers continued to reduce their inventory levels.

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit $2,282M, up 38% YoY, on the ramp of Instinct MI300 GPUs and 4th Gen EPYC CPUs — while Embedded fell 24% to $1,057M as customers worked through inventory.
takeaways.title: Data Center carried the quarter

takeaways.text: GAAP net income was $667M, but $297M of it was an income-tax benefit rather than operating performance; operating income itself was $342M, a 6% margin. Non-GAAP net income was $1,249M.
takeaways.title: A tax benefit flattered profit

takeaways.text: Client revenue rose 62% YoY to $1,461M on Ryzen 7000 Series sales as the PC market recovered; Gaming fell 17% to $1,368M on weaker semi-custom revenue.
takeaways.title: PC chips bounced back

verdict: AMD's revenue rose 10% to $6.2B as record AI GPU and server-chip sales outran a weak embedded market, and a $297M tax benefit lifted net income to $667M.
